papers.title: Structural diversity of new mixed-ligand Ni(ii) complexes derived from ciprofloxacin and 2-methylbenzimidazole: synthesis, characterization, DFT insights, antimicrobial activity and DNA gyrase B (4DUH) docking.
papers.abstract: A set of mixed ligand nickel(ii) complexes, namely, NiAC ([Ni(CIP)(MIM)(OAc)]), NiPE ([Ni(CIP)(MIM)(H2O)]ClO4), and NiCL([Ni(CIP)(MIM)(H2O)2Cl]), derived from the combination of ciprofloxacin (CIP) and 2-methylbenzimidazole (MIM), were synthesized in high yields (85-88%) and characterized by various physicochemical as well as computational techniques. The 1 : 1 : 1 stoichiometry was established by elemental analysis, whereas the non-electrolytic nature of the complexes was established by the molar conductance studies for NiAC (9.62 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1) and NiCL (10.85 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1), in comparison t
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of three new mixed-ligand nickel(II) complexes combining ciprofloxacin and 2-methylbenzimidazole, using spectroscopic, computational (DFT), and biological methods. The complexes were tested for antimicrobial activity and docked against DNA gyrase B (PDB 4DUH), suggesting a potential mechanism of action. The work is primarily a coordination chemistry study with preliminary biological evaluation.

papers.title: Multiobjective Fluorescent Molecule Design with a Data-Physics Dual-Driven Generative Framework.
papers.abstract: Designing fluorescent small molecules requires simultaneous control over optical responses, brightness, and physicochemical constraints across vast, underexplored chemical spaces. Conventional generate-score-screen approaches become impractical under such realistic design specifications, owing to their low search efficiency, unreliable generalizability of machine-learning predictions, and the prohibitive cost of quantum chemical calculations. Here, we present LUMOS, a data- and physics-driven framework for inverse design of fluorescent molecules. LUMOS couples the generator and predictor withi
papers.summary: LUMOS is a generative framework for inverse design of fluorescent small molecules that couples a molecular generator with property predictors in a data- and physics-driven loop, avoiding the inefficient generate-score-screen paradigm. It aims to simultaneously satisfy multiple objectives such as optical response, brightness, and physicochemical constraints while reducing reliance on costly quantum chemical calculations.

papers.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Oxidation Resistance for Tertiary Phosphines Using Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potential-Aided Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Tertiary phosphines play important roles in a wide range of chemical reactions, but they suffer from oxidation in air. Here, we propose a computational workflow for the comprehensive prediction of oxidation resistance in tertiary phosphines based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using Matlantis PFP, a universal machine learning interatomic potential (uMLIP). MD simulations were conducted for 51 different tertiary phosphines and analyzed to estimate mean survival time by survival analysis (τ). The resulting τ reproduced experimentally and theoretically recognized trends in oxidation resis
papers.summary: This paper introduces a computational workflow that uses a universal machine learning interatomic potential (Matlantis PFP) combined with molecular dynamics simulations to predict the oxidation resistance of tertiary phosphines. By simulating 51 different tertiary phosphines and applying survival analysis to estimate mean survival times, the approach reproduces known experimental and theoretical trends in oxidation resistance. This offers a scalable, simulation-based method for screening phosphine stability without extensive experimental testing.

papers.title: Bridging Visual Intuition and Chemical Expertise: A Virtual Collaborative Framework for Autonomous Nonadiabatic Dynamics Analysis.
papers.abstract: Analyzing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics trajectories traditionally heavily relies on expert intuition and visual pattern recognition, a process that is difficult to formalize. We present VisU, a vision-driven framework that leverages the complementary strengths of two state-of-the-art large language models (Doubao-Seed-1.6-Vision and DeepSeek-V3.2) to establish a "virtual research cooperation". This operates through a "Mentor-Engineer-Student" paradigm that mimics the collaborative intelligence of a professional chemistry laboratory. Within this ecosystem, the Mentor provides physical intuit
papers.summary: The authors present VisU, a vision-driven framework that uses two large language models in a 'Mentor-Engineer-Student' paradigm to autonomously analyze nonadiabatic molecular dynamics trajectories, a task traditionally requiring expert visual intuition. This virtual research collaboration aims to formalize and automate the interpretation of complex chemical dynamics data.

papers.title: Conformational Preference Classification of Integrin-Binding Ligands Using Free Energy Perturbation.
papers.abstract: Integrins are crucial cell adhesion receptors and attractive therapeutic targets, but developing safe small-molecule inhibitors has been challenging, at least in part due to inadvertent partial agonism caused by stabilization of the integrin's open, high-affinity state. To address this challenge, we present a computational approach using Absolute Binding Free Energy Perturbation (AB-FEP) calculations to predict whether a ligand will stabilize the open or closed integrin states, leveraging the difference between the ligand's binding free energy to the respective end states. Despite challenges p
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method using Absolute Binding Free Energy Perturbation (AB-FEP) calculations to predict whether small-molecule ligands will stabilize the open (active) or closed (inactive) conformation of integrins. By comparing a ligand's binding free energy to each end state, the approach aims to help design safer integrin inhibitors that avoid unintended partial agonism. The work addresses a key challenge in developing therapeutic integrin-targeting drugs.

papers.title: Enhanced Sampling of Protein Conformations in AlphaFold3 with Repulsive Bias in the Diffusion Generative Model.
papers.abstract: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3 (AF3), to predict. It has been observed that AF3 sometimes fails to capture ligand-induced conformational changes, even though it explicitly includes ligand molecules that induce such changes. To address this challenge, we develop an enhanced sampling scheme that leverages the diffusion-based generative model used in AF3 to predict protein structures. Interpreting the diffusion generative model as a stochastic sampling process analogous to molec
papers.summary: The authors introduce an enhanced sampling method that adds a repulsive bias to AlphaFold3's diffusion-based structure prediction, allowing it to explore alternative protein conformations rather than collapsing to a single predicted state. This addresses AF3's known limitation in capturing ligand-induced conformational changes, even when the ligand is explicitly provided. The approach reframes AF3's diffusion model as a stochastic sampler analogous to molecular dynamics, enabling broader conformational exploration.

papers.title: Quinazoline-tethered thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors: green synthesis, molecular docking, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-fused heterocycles have attracted considerable research interest in pharmaceutical, medicinal, organometallic, and materials chemistry. In this work, two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives were synthesized using choline hydroxide as an environmentally friendly catalyst. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT). Compound 11e showed the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 0.599 µg mL-1 (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was performed to examine
papers.summary: This paper reports the green synthesis of two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives using choline hydroxide as an eco-friendly catalyst. The compounds were tested against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase, with compound 11e showing the strongest inhibition (IC50 = 0.599 µg/mL). Molecular docking studies were used to explore how these compounds bind to the enzyme.

papers.title: Electronic structure-performance relationship in pyridine-based Schiff bases: a dual experimental-DFT study on corrosion inhibition.
papers.abstract: Two pyridine-based Schiff bases, N-(4-bromobenzylidene)pyridin-3-amine (BBPA) and N-[4-(dimethylamino)benzylidene]pyridin-3-amine (DBPA), were synthesized and evaluated as corrosion inhibitors for carbon steel in 1.0 M HCl. Their inhibition performance was investigated using potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and electrochemical frequency modulation (EFM). Both compounds exhibited excellent corrosion protection, achieving inhibition efficiencies above 94% at 10 mM concentration. Adsorption studies revealed that the inhibitors obey the Langmuir iso
papers.summary: Two pyridine-based Schiff bases (BBPA and DBPA) were synthesized and tested as corrosion inhibitors for carbon steel in acidic solution, achieving over 94% inhibition efficiency at 10 mM. The study combines electrochemical experiments with DFT calculations to link electronic structure features to inhibition performance, with adsorption following the Langmuir isotherm.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and preliminary anticancer evaluation of diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives: in vitro, in vivo and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer-associated mortality and morbidity worldwide, and there is a continued need for structurally diverse anticancer agents with improved properties. The present study reports a series of diphenylpropan-1-one (DPP) derivatives (4a-4i), rationally designed around a chalcone framework and synthesized via a three-step reaction sequence. The physicochemical and spectral characterization of the synthesized derivatives was performed using spectral techniques. Their anticancer potential was evaluated through a preliminary in vitro cytotoxicity screening against t
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of nine diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives based on a chalcone scaffold, followed by preliminary anticancer testing. The compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against breast cancer cells in vitro, with additional in vivo and in silico analyses. The work aims to identify structurally diverse anticancer candidates with potential for further development.

papers.title: Site-Specific Features Guiding Effective Reversible Photocontrol of Tryptophan Synthase With the Unnatural Amino Acid AzoF.
papers.abstract: This study delivers initial guidelines for the selection of effective incorporation positions for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF to facilitate the successful engineering of light-sensitive enzymes, dubbed photoxenases. Although photoxenases gain interest for the photocontrol of enzymatic activity across various fields their design has so far remained challenging. To ease particularly the selection of AzoF incorporation sites, we have systematically evaluated a total of 85 positions that differ in their biochemical and biophysical features in the bi-enzyme model system tryptopha
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates 85 different incorporation sites for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF in tryptophan synthase to identify rules for engineering light-controllable enzymes (photoxenases). The authors provide initial guidelines on which site-specific biochemical and biophysical features favor effective reversible photocontrol of enzymatic activity.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors present MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also introduce MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrate that the model can guide rational enzyme evolution.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review argues that GPCRs function in the brain as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes rather than as isolated monomers, challenging the conventional drug discovery paradigm. The authors synthesize evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and pharmacology to suggest that targeting GPCR heteromers could improve treatments for neuropsychiatric disorders where current drugs show limited efficacy or resistance.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening followed by in vitro testing to identify HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups, aiming to overcome the poor selectivity and pharmacokinetic issues of traditional hydroxamate inhibitors. The authors prioritized compounds forming HDAC3-specific interactions and bidentate/monodentate zinc coordination. The work demonstrates a criteria-guided strategy for developing more selective epigenetic inhibitors.

papers.title: [Rational design for improving the thermostability of β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans].
papers.abstract: The β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans (Bgl52) has been identified as a thermophilic and acidophilic β-glucosidase, which constitutes the most critical component in the cellulolytic enzyme system for cellulose hydrolysis. Although Bgl52 is a thermophilic enzyme, its poor thermal stability at high temperatures restricts its long-term industrial application under elevated-temperature conditions. In this study, rational design strategies, including two free energy calculation programs (Fireprot and FoldX) and homologous sequence alignment, were integrated to perform single-point and mu
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study applied rational design strategies—combining free energy calculation tools (FireProt and FoldX) with homologous sequence alignment—to engineer the thermophilic β-glucosidase Bgl52 from Bacillus thermoamylovorans for improved thermal stability. The goal was to overcome the enzyme's poor stability at high temperatures, which limits its long-term industrial use in cellulose hydrolysis. The work demonstrates a computational protein engineering pipeline for enhancing enzyme thermostability.

papers.title: [Rational design and molecular engineering of a chitosanase for preparing specific chito-oligosaccharides with degree of polymerization≥5].
papers.abstract: To achieve efficient enzymatic preparation of specific high-degree-of-polymerization chito-oligosaccharides (degree of polymerization≥5, DP≥5), rational molecular engineering of chitosanase Csn46-Mut4 was performed in this study. Through site-directed mutagenesis coupled with DNS enzyme activity-HPLC product distribution screening, a superior mutant, C41A/T47A/V144A, was obtained. Under conditions of 55℃ and pH 5.5, the catalytic efficiency and thermostability of this enzyme were remarkably enhanced, reaching 2.56-fold and 1.67-fold those of Csn46-Mut4, respectively. Peak area normalization an
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used rational design and site-directed mutagenesis to engineer a chitosanase (Csn46-Mut4) into a superior triple mutant (C41A/T47A/V144A) that produces chito-oligosaccharides with a degree of polymerization of 5 or higher. The engineered enzyme showed 2.56-fold higher catalytic efficiency and 1.67-fold improved thermostability compared to the parent enzyme, enabling more efficient preparation of these specific oligosaccharides.

papers.title: A water-pinning hotspot drives templated tau aggregation.
papers.abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured sol
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, forms seed-competent fibrils that propagate between cells in tauopathies. The authors identify a single dominant 'water-pinning' hotspot that drives in-register stacking of tau molecules onto fibril seeds, preventing mismatched aggregation. This mechanism may explain the templated, prion-like spread of tau pathology.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTAC molecules, which are therapeutic compounds that degrade target proteins via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, addressing key limitations in PROTAC design. This enables more controllable and drug-like PROTAC candidate generation.

papers.title: Targeting DYRK1A with rationally designed pyrazine-guanidine hybrids for Alzheimer's disease: design, synthesis, and biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Dual-specificity tyrosine phosphorylation-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) has been implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) by regulating tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammatory pathways, suggesting DYRK1A as an important therapeutic target. Herein, we report the rational design, synthesis and evaluation of a new class of low-molecular-weight pyrazine-guanidine molecular hybrids as potential DYRK1A inhibitors via an integrated computational and experimental approach. Molecular docking studies predicted good protein-ligand interactions, with compounds F1, F5, and F7 exhibi
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrazine-guanidine hybrid molecules intended to inhibit DYRK1A, a kinase implicated in Alzheimer's disease through tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammation. Using molecular docking followed by experimental evaluation, compounds F1, F5, and F7 showed promising binding interactions and biological activity, suggesting these hybrids could serve as leads for AD therapeutics.

papers.title: Evolutionary Dynamics-Aware De Novo Design of a Thermostable NS1-Derived Diagnostic Protein for Yellow Fever Virus.
papers.abstract: Serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses remains hindered by extensive intra-genus cross-reactivity, compromising both assay specificity and epidemiological accuracy. In this study, we focused on yellow fever virus (YFV) as a model system to design and validate a generalizable de novo protein design framework integrating evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to rationally engineer diagnostic antigens with reduced cross-reactivity and improved cost-effectiveness. Through comprehensive evolutionary mapping over time of the YFV polyprotein, we identified conserved yet discriminator
papers.summary: The authors developed a de novo protein design framework that combines evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to engineer a thermostable diagnostic antigen derived from yellow fever virus NS1, aiming to reduce cross-reactivity with related flaviviruses. By mapping evolutionary conservation across the YFV polyprotein, they identified discriminating regions for rational antigen design. This work offers a generalizable approach for improving serological diagnostics of neglected arboviruses.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Design of Metal-Phenolic Networks: From Precision Assembly to Multidimensional Synergistic Therapy for Brain Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Brain disorders, such as glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and ischemic stroke, represent formidable challenges due to the highly restrictive blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex pathophysiological microenvironment, which severely compromise drug delivery and therapeutic outcomes. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), as a class of novel hybrid materials, hold great promise for overcoming brain delivery bottlenecks and enabling precise synergistic therapy by leveraging their unique physicochemical properties. However, a comprehensive synthesis of MPN designs tailored specifically to
papers.summary: This review discusses metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), a class of hybrid materials, as a strategy for overcoming the blood-brain barrier and treating brain disorders like glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and ischemic stroke. It synthesizes design principles for MPNs, from precision assembly to multidimensional synergistic therapy, highlighting their potential for improved brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Molecular glues: Recent advances in cereblon substrate identification and mechanistic insights.
papers.abstract: This highlight summarizes the recent advances in cereblon (CRBN) substrate discovery and mechanisms of action within the field of molecular glues. It emphasizes that molecular glue technology has transitioned from the stage of monofunctional targeted protein degradation to that of rational design and multidimensional regulation. Key recent breakthroughs include: (1) overcoming the limitations of canonical CRBN recognition motifs, identifying extensive novel substrates and unconventional recognition modes independent of fixed specific secondary structures; (2) reconceptualizing G protein-couple
papers.summary: This highlight reviews recent progress in understanding how molecular glues recruit the E3 ligase cereblon (CRBN) to degrade target proteins. It emphasizes a shift from serendipitous monofunctional degradation toward rational design, including discovery of novel CRBN substrates and unconventional recognition modes that do not rely on canonical structural motifs.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase (mTS) will produce linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic) by using active site properties as features rather than sequence alone. The approach addresses the difficulty of engineering these enzymes by capturing structure-function relationships that sequence-based methods miss.

papers.title: Morphology Evolution and Structural Reorganization of Enzyme-Biosurfactant Systems: Implications for Petroleum Interfacial Engineering.
papers.abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable chemical solutions in petroleum engineering has catalyzed the development of bio-based formulations characterized by high interfacial activity and low environmental toxicity. This study investigates the intermolecular interactions and structural evolution within composite systems comprising representative glycolipid biosurfactants and carbohydrate hydrolases. Rheological and light scattering assessments reveal that the introduction of enzymes triggers a transition from large-scale micelles to highly dispersed micro-aggregates, accompanied by a significant
papers.summary: This study examines how adding carbohydrate hydrolase enzymes to glycolipid biosurfactants changes the system's structure, causing a shift from large micelles to smaller, dispersed micro-aggregates. These findings suggest enzyme-biosurfactant combinations could improve interfacial performance in petroleum engineering applications.

papers.title: High-throughput physics-based enzyme engineering.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering aims to tailor natural enzymes for industrial and therapeutic applications, yet physically grounded rational design has been limited by a trade-off between accuracy and cost, leaving the field heavily dependent on expert intuition. Here we present a scalable physics-based framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to capture enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while enabling efficient, atomistic exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes. Coupled with microkinetic modelling, the framework translates molecular free-energ
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present a scalable physics-based enzyme engineering framework that couples field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to model enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. Combined with microkinetic modeling, it enables high-throughput exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes, reducing reliance on expert intuition for rational enzyme design.

papers.title: Engineered mRNA nanostructures expand the design space of mRNA therapeutics through programmable protein expression and immune stimulation.
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have transformed vaccination and protein replacement strategies, yet efforts to improve their performance have focused largely on sequence engineering, nucleotide modification, and delivery vehicles. Here we show that mRNA function can be controlled by rational design of higher-order RNA architectures. We develop self-assembling mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of unimolecular RNA nanostructures that encode protein-coding sequences within higher-order, programmable, and compact nucleic acid architectures. Using computational design and experimental validation,
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of self-assembling, unimolecular RNA nanostructures that embed protein-coding sequences within programmable higher-order architectures. By rationally designing RNA structure rather than only tuning sequence, modification, or delivery, the authors show that mRNA function—including protein expression and immune stimulation—can be controlled through architectural design. This expands the design space for mRNA therapeutics beyond conventional sequence engineering.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This paper introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that replaces the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation, paired with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. Evaluated on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline, the work tests whether adaptive nonlinear function learning improves affinity prediction for virtual screening and lead optimization.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates the current state of molecular docking studies on natural products, highlighting widespread methodological variability and the lack of standardized guidelines. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets require tailored docking approaches, and proposes practical recommendations to improve rigor and reproducibility in the field.

papers.title: Unveiling Novel Metalloprotease Inhibitors Targeting Botulinum Neurotoxin Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Drug Libraries and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) is one of the most lethal biological substances to humans, which inhibits acetylcholine release by the presynaptic nerve in neuromuscular junctions. Of the existing BoNT serotypes, BoNT serotype A (BoNT/A) is particularly potent, making it the primary focus in neurotoxin research. Its catalytic domain exhibits similar structural features and zinc-dependent activity as thermolysin, a key bacterial enzyme, which provides a foundation for designing antibacterial agents targeting related protease mechanisms. Repurposing of preapproved drugs or existing medications has r
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of existing drug libraries combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify novel metalloprotease inhibitors targeting the catalytic domain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A. The work leverages the structural similarity between BoNT/A and thermolysin to repurpose approved drugs as potential therapeutics against this highly lethal neurotoxin.

papers.title: Dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-ones and Benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-ones: Useful Scaffolds for Development of Protein-Protein Interaction Inhibitors †.
papers.abstract: Modulation of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) by small molecules is a vital strategy in drug discovery. Nevertheless, due to the inherent nature of PPI interfaces, practical implementation of this approach remains a high-hanging fruit in medicinal chemistry. In this report, we develop a new line of PEX14-PEX5 PPI inhibitors by homologation of a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold. The challenging chemistry of 8-membered ring formation led to the development of novel PEX14 inhibitors featuring a 6+8+6 tricyclic system. The obtained analogs were tested for their capabi
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis of novel dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-one and benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-one scaffolds as inhibitors of the PEX14-PEX5 protein-protein interaction. By homologating a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold, the authors created 6+8+6 tricyclic compounds that were tested for PPI inhibitory activity. The work provides new chemical scaffolds for developing PPI inhibitors, a challenging area in drug discovery.

papers.title: Inhibitor fluorination pattern modulates protein surface dynamics and chemically induced dimerization.
papers.abstract: Chemically induced proximity is a powerful strategy to regulate cellular processes using small-molecule ligands that act as "molecular glues" to influence the lifetime, localization, and function of biological targets. However, the structure-activity relationships governing such inducible interactions remain elusive. Here, using a series of self-assembling homodimerizers that target an essential parasitic redox enzyme, we present a systematic, fluorination-guided strategy to tune induced protein homodimer affinity by two orders of magnitude. Combining NMR spectroscopy, MD simulations, chromato
papers.summary: This study shows that adding fluorine atoms to inhibitor molecules can tune how strongly they glue two copies of a parasite redox enzyme together, changing induced dimerization affinity by up to 100-fold. Using NMR spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors reveal that fluorination alters protein surface dynamics, providing a general strategy for designing better chemically induced dimerization tools.

papers.title: Optimization of dsRNA Length and Target Position for Enhanced RNA Interference Efficiency Targeting the Chitinase Gene MsChi2 in Mythimna separata.
papers.abstract: Chitinase is a key enzyme involved in insect chitin metabolism, and RNA interference (RNAi) targeting the corresponding gene represents a promising strategy for eco-friendly pest management. However, the design parameters of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), particularly fragment length and target position, remain insufficiently optimized. To investigate the effects of these parameters on the RNAi efficiency against the MsChi2 gene in Mythimna separata, we synthesized four dsRNAs of 60, 200, 500, and 1000 bp and administered them to larvae. The results indicated that 200 and 500 bp dsRNAs significa
papers.summary: This study tested how the length and target position of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) affect RNA interference efficiency against the chitinase gene MsChi2 in the armyworm Mythimna separata. They found that 200 and 500 bp dsRNA fragments significantly improved knockdown compared to 60 and 1000 bp fragments, suggesting an optimal intermediate length for pest control applications.

papers.title: Comprehensive Characterization of Cytochrome P450s Reveals Candidate Enzymes Involved in the Metabolic Fate of Absorbed Volatile Organic Compounds in Potato.
papers.abstract: Plants are continuously exposed to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted by neighbors. Although the mechanisms governing VOC uptake and metabolism remain unclear, cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYP450s) are thought to participate in the detoxification and metabolic conversion of absorbed VOCs. Data from previously conducted cDNA microarray transcriptomic profiling in potato exposed to French marigold essential oil (FM-EO) was here used to filter differentially expressed sequences, and identified 54 unique CYP450 transcripts. Among the 10 most highly expressed sequences, two CYP81D1-like (
papers.summary: This study used transcriptomic profiling of potato plants exposed to French marigold essential oil to identify 54 differentially expressed cytochrome P450 genes, narrowing to 10 highly expressed candidates. Two CYP81D1-like enzymes emerged as likely participants in the detoxification and metabolic conversion of absorbed volatile organic compounds.

papers.title: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence in Antibody Design: From Structure-Based Engineering to Generative Models.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed computational antibody engineering by enabling accurate prediction of antibody structures, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design. Recent advances in deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI have fundamentally changed the way antibodies are discovered and engineered. This review aims to present the historical evolution of computational antibody engineering, from early structure-based design strategies to modern AI-driven approaches, while highlighting the major computation
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of computational antibody engineering from early structure-based design methods to modern AI-driven approaches, including deep learning, protein language models, and generative models. It highlights how these advances now enable accurate antibody structure prediction, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design.

papers.title: Rational Design of Aspergillus awamori Glucoamylase for Activity Improvement.
papers.abstract: Glucoamylases are highly demanded by the industry for starch saccharification, which necessitates an increase in enzyme activity. To improve the activity of Aspergillus awamori VKPM F-1262 glucoamylase N181Q (AGAM), amino acid substitutions were made in the region of substrate binding. In the case of the variant D237G, there was a 1.3-1.4-fold increase in activity towards soluble starch for the individual enzyme and crude enzyme solution after cultivation in flasks. For the variants G57A and C319T, there was also a 1.1-1.4-fold increase in enzyme activity for the crude flask solution, while th
papers.summary: This study rationally engineered Aspergillus awamori glucoamylase by introducing amino acid substitutions in the substrate-binding region to improve starch saccharification activity. The D237G variant showed a 1.3–1.4-fold activity increase toward soluble starch, while G57A and C319T also improved activity in crude enzyme solutions. These modest gains suggest targeted mutations can enhance industrial enzyme performance.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: The authors present a fast structural search method to classify gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. Their approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods like CLEAN and ProteInter, which struggle with closely related enzyme functions, and on alignment-based structural methods that produce high false positive rates for globally similar proteins.

papers.title: Discovery and molecular insights of a novel pea-derived antioxidant peptide: From quantum chemical insights to oxidative stability of walnut oil.
papers.abstract: This study identified novel antioxidant peptides from defeasated pea protein and characterized their molecular properties and protective effects in a lipid system. Following ultrafiltration, Sephadex G-15 purification, Nano LC-MS/MS identification, and in silico screening, five unreported peptides (F1-F5) were selected for evaluation. Antioxidant activities varied across DPPH, ABTS, and hydroxyl radical assays, reflecting sequence- and assay-specific differences. Integrated experimental and computational analyses identified GIPYWTY (F1) as the lead peptide. Molecular docking revealed favorable
papers.summary: This study identified five novel antioxidant peptides from pea protein using ultrafiltration, chromatography, mass spectrometry, and computational screening. The lead peptide GIPYWTY showed strong antioxidant activity and was characterized molecularly via docking and quantum chemical analysis, with demonstrated protective effects on walnut oil oxidative stability.

papers.title: Exploring the Neuropharmacological Potential of Ligustrum sinense Relevant to Parkinson's Disease: In Vivo and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are valuable sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders. This study investigated the antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities of Ligustrum sinense (L. sinense) leaf extract through in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. Antioxidant activity assessed by the DPPH assay demonstrated moderate free radical scavenging capacity (IC50 = 73.56 ± 2.18 µg/mL) compared with l-ascorbic acid (IC50 = 7.29 ± 2.86 µg/mL). Behavioral evaluations using the open field, hole cross, elevated plus maze,
papers.summary: This study evaluates leaf extracts of the medicinal plant Ligustrum sinense for antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities using in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches, with relevance to Parkinson's disease. The extract showed moderate antioxidant activity and behavioral effects in rodent models, with computational docking suggesting interactions with MAO targets. The findings support further investigation of L. sinense as a source of neuroactive compounds, though the antioxidant potency was modest compared to standard ascorbic acid.

papers.title: Multi-Omics and Computational Pharmacology Approach With Experimental Validation Reveals the Antiproliferative Activity of Sophoricoside Against Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer has a dismal prognosis and limited therapeutic options, highlighting an urgent need for effective treatments. Sophoricoside (SOP), a natural isoflavone glycoside, has exhibited anticancer activities in multiple malignancies, including lung cancer, glioblastoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma. We combined cellular assays, network pharmacology, machine learning, and multi-omics to investigate SOP's effects. SOP-inhibited proliferation of MIA PaCa-2, SW1990, and PANC-1 cells dose-dependently. Network pharmacology revealed 85 overlapping targets enriched in MAPK, apoptosis, and PD-
papers.summary: This study investigates sophoricoside (SOP), a natural isoflavone glycoside, for its anticancer activity against pancreatic cancer. Using cellular assays, network pharmacology, machine learning, and multi-omics, the authors found that SOP inhibits proliferation of multiple pancreatic cancer cell lines and identified 85 overlapping targets enriched in MAPK and apoptosis pathways. The work provides experimental validation of SOP's antiproliferative effects and potential mechanisms.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell Transcriptomics, Multi-Omics Analyses, and Computational Pharmacology Reveal Macrophage Heterogeneity and the Putative THBS1-CD36 Axis in Coronary Atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Coronary atherosclerosis (CA) is characterized by profound macrophage heterogeneity that drives plaque progression and vulnerability, yet the precise subpopulations and their niche-specific functions remain incompletely defined. Here, we constructed a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human CA using dataset GSE131778 and identified six distinct macrophage subpopulations. Among these, the THBS1+ macrophage subset emerged as a terminally differentiated, hypoxia-adaptive population with elevated TGF-β signaling and FOSB-driven transcriptional regulation. High-dimensional weighted gene co-expres
papers.summary: This study built a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human coronary atherosclerosis and identified six macrophage subpopulations, with a THBS1+ subset emerging as a terminally differentiated, hypoxia-adaptive population linked to TGF-β signaling and FOSB-driven regulation. Integrative multi-omics and computational pharmacology analyses further point to a putative THBS1-CD36 axis as a potential therapeutic target in plaque progression.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Single-Cell Analyses Implicate NOX4 as an Icariin-Associated Oxidative Stress Regulatory Node in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Icariin, a prenylated flavonoid glycoside from Epimedium species, is a representative dietary polyphenol with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antitumor properties. Gastric cancer (GC) is a major non-communicable chronic disease characterized by complex molecular alterations and dysregulated redox homeostasis, yet the molecular targets underlying the potential anti-GC activity of icariin remain poorly defined. In this study, we integrated network pharmacology, bulk transcriptomic analysis (TCGA-STAD; GSE15497, GSE84437, GSE84433, and GSE26253), and single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE183904; 142
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, bulk transcriptomic data from multiple gastric cancer cohorts, and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify molecular targets of the dietary flavonoid icariin in gastric cancer. The authors pinpoint NOX4, an NADPH oxidase involved in reactive oxygen species production, as a key oxidative stress regulatory node associated with icariin's potential anti-gastric cancer effects.

papers.title: State-dependent inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels by DCPIB.
papers.abstract: DCPIB is the prototypical inhibitor of leucine-rich repeat containing protein 8 volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs), yet the structural basis and state dependence of inhibition remain unclear. Here, we used chimeric channels, targeted mutagenesis, and electrophysiology to define the determinants of DCPIB inhibition and elucidate how drug binding is coupled to channel gating. Effective inhibition required coordinated contributions from extracellular loop 1 (EL1) and transmembrane domain 2 (TM2), which together form a functional module governing access to and stabilization of DCPIB-bound sta
papers.summary: This study uses chimeric channels, targeted mutagenesis, and electrophysiology to identify how the inhibitor DCPIB blocks LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels. The authors show that inhibition depends on coordinated contributions from extracellular loop 1 and transmembrane domain 2, which together control drug access and stabilize a drug-bound state, revealing that DCPIB inhibition is state-dependent.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that binds GSTP1 and enhances its catalytic activity in biochemical assays. Since GSTP1 is often silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma, chemically boosting residual enzyme activity could offer a new therapeutic angle for prostate cancer.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis prioritizes ALDH2 as a candidate Puerarin-associated target linked to macrophage infiltration in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Puerarin is a bioactive isoflavone with reported anti-tumor and immunomodulatory activities; however, its candidate molecular targets and associations with the immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD) remain incompletely defined. This study integrated computational analyses with a murine LUAD model to prioritize candidate puerarin-associated targets and evaluate their relationships with immune-cell changes.
papers.summary: This study integrates computational multi-omics analyses with a murine lung adenocarcinoma model to identify candidate molecular targets of puerarin, an isoflavone with reported anti-tumor activity. ALDH2 emerged as a prioritized puerarin-associated target, and its expression was linked to macrophage infiltration in the tumor immune microenvironment. The findings suggest a potential mechanistic connection between puerarin, ALDH2, and immune cell dynamics in LUAD.

papers.title: Identification of natural TLR4 modulators through network pharmacology and molecular modeling in SARS-CoV-2 Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection.
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii exacerbates hyperinflammation via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated immune pathways. Using network pharmacology, an integrated protein-protein interaction network identified 30 key inter-species hubs comprising viral, bacterial, and human host proteins, with TLR4 achieving a high MCC score (722), highlighting its high topological centrality as a host immune target. Virtual screen of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex identified three top candidates, CID5898023, CID5403474, and CID74977829, with docki
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify TLR4 as a central host immune hub in SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection, then virtually screens 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex. Three top candidate compounds (CID5898023, CID5403474, CID74977829) were identified with favorable docking scores, suggesting potential natural modulators of TLR4-driven hyperinflammation.

papers.title: HIST1H2BJ is associated with poor prognosis and an immune-altered tumor microenvironment in glioma.
papers.abstract: Glioma, the most prevalent and aggressive primary malignant brain tumor, is associated with poor clinical outcomes. There is an urgent need for novel biomarkers to predict survival and therapeutic response, as existing markers offer limited prognostic utility.
papers.summary: This study identifies HIST1H2BJ, a histone gene, as a biomarker associated with poor prognosis in glioma patients. The authors also link its expression to an altered tumor immune microenvironment, suggesting it may influence how gliomas interact with the immune system. These findings point to HIST1H2BJ as a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic target worth further investigation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analysis reveals a convergent cholangiocyte-associated host inflammatory program in biliary atresia and SARS-CoV-2-associated hepatobiliary injury.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2-associated hepatobiliary injury and biliary atresia (BA) differ markedly in etiology and biological context, but both involve injury to the biliary epithelial compartment. Here, we performed integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analyses to investigate whether these distinct hepatobiliary injury contexts converge on a shared cholangiocyte-associated inflammatory host-response program. Bulk transcriptomic datasets from SARS-CoV-2-infected human liver organoids and BA liver tissues were integrated to identify shared transcriptional alterations, followed by functional enrichment,
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic data from SARS-CoV-2-infected liver organoids and biliary atresia (BA) liver tissue, combined with single-cell analysis, to test whether two very different biliary injury contexts converge on a shared cholangiocyte-driven inflammatory program. The authors identify a common host inflammatory response signature centered on cholangiocytes, suggesting conserved injury-response mechanisms across distinct hepatobiliary diseases.

papers.title: Mechanistic Evaluation of LolA and β-Sliding Clamp Inhibition by Silybin and Diclofenac as Gentamicin Adjuvants Against Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli.
papers.abstract: To address the challenges of antimicrobial resistance, one potential approach is to repurpose existing drugs. In the current study, structurally distinct antibiotics were combined with the repurposed drugs silybin and diclofenac to evaluate the potential of these combinations against resistant bacterial strains. The investigation encompassed in vitro determination of the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and time-kill kinetics, as well as in vivo assessments of percentage change in body weight, total white blood cell (WBC) count, colitis and edema, histopathological changes, stool scores,
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether two repurposed drugs, silybin and diclofenac, can enhance gentamicin's activity against enteropathogenic Escherichia coli, using both in vitro assays (MIC, time-kill kinetics) and in vivo animal models of infection and inflammation. The authors also perform mechanistic analyses suggesting inhibition of LolA and the β-sliding clamp as possible targets. The work supports drug repurposing as a strategy to overcome antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: An integrated network toxicology and multi-omics framework prioritizes BRCA1 as a testable candidate in benzo[a]pyrene-associated oral cancer.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposure to benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) is a recognized risk factor for oral cancer, but systematic strategies for prioritizing candidate molecular nodes and generating experimentally testable hypotheses remain limited. Here, we conducted a hypothesis-generating, methodologically oriented exploratory study using an integrated three-tier framework comprising computational target prioritization, multi-omics contextualization, and preliminary phenotypic assessment. Network toxicology identified four genes shared between the predefined BaP-associated and oral cancer-related gene sets: EGFR,
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology with multi-omics data to prioritize candidate genes linking benzo[a]pyrene exposure to oral cancer, identifying four shared genes including BRCA1 and EGFR. The framework is presented as a hypothesis-generating approach for nominating testable molecular targets in environmental carcinogenesis.

papers.title: Rational discovery of peptide inhibitors targeting Keap1: a focus on neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1)/Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) pathway is a promising therapeutic target for neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs). Nrf2 activation mitigates key pathogenic mechanisms in NDDs by enhancing antioxidant defenses, suppressing neuroinflammation, improving mitochondrial function, inhibiting ferroptosis, and maintaining proteostasis.
papers.summary: This paper describes a rational computational approach to discover peptide inhibitors that target Keap1, aiming to activate the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway as a therapeutic strategy for neurodegenerative diseases. The work highlights Keap1/Nrf2 as a promising target and proposes peptides as a modality to modulate it.

papers.title: ProNA3D: Distance-Based Analysis of Nucleic Acid-Containing Interfaces.
papers.abstract: Biomolecular interactions are central to many essential cellular processes, but RNA-containing complexes remain challenging to resolve structurally, even as experimental methods and AI-based prediction have expanded structural coverage. Tools for the integrated analysis of interfaces within such complexes remain limited. We present ProNA3D, a tool that provides a unified platform for analyzing protein-nucleic acid and nucleic acid-only complexes, bridging the gap between structure prediction and functional interpretation. ProNA3D supports both experimental and computationally predicted structu
papers.summary: ProNA3D is a new computational tool that provides a unified platform for analyzing interfaces in protein-nucleic acid and nucleic acid-only complexes, using distance-based metrics. It works with both experimental structures and AI-predicted models, helping bridge the gap between structure prediction and functional interpretation for RNA-containing complexes that remain difficult to resolve experimentally.

papers.title: Preclinical Simulation of Transoral Robotic Thyroidectomy Using a Training Box and the Versius Robotic Platform.
papers.abstract: Transoral robotic thyroidectomy (TORT) represents an alternative to open surgery, offering favorable cosmetic outcomes and comparable oncologic results. However, standardized training pathways and validated simulation models replicating standardized setups for emerging robotic platforms remain limited. An experimental simulation of total thyroidectomy and central (recurrent) neck dissection was performed with the Versius robotic system in a validated synthetic training box. Optimal robotic positioning and docking were determined, and a standardized procedural sequence was followed to ensure op
papers.summary: This study developed a preclinical simulation model for transoral robotic thyroidectomy using the Versius robotic platform and a synthetic training box. The authors defined optimal robotic docking positions and a standardized procedural sequence for total thyroidectomy and central neck dissection. The work provides a structured training pathway for surgeons learning this minimally invasive technique on a new robotic system.

papers.title: Analyzing the cytotoxicity and pro-tumorigenic role of acetyl tributyl citrate in prostate through network toxicology and the immune microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) is an alternative plasticizer to Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) and bisphenol A (BPA) that may contribute to the development of various cancers. The cytotoxic activity and pro-tumorigenic role of ATBC in prostate cancer (PCa) progression remains poorly understood, highlighting the need for a systematic evaluation of its molecular toxicity.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology combined with immune microenvironment analysis to investigate how the plasticizer acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) may contribute to prostate cancer progression. The authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways linking ATBC exposure to cytotoxicity and pro-tumorigenic effects, suggesting ATBC is not a harmless substitute for DEHP and BPA.

papers.title: Extra-nasal odorant receptors: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Since the first demonstration of extra-nasal odorant receptor (OR) function of OR1D2 (hOR17-4) in human sperm, ORs have emerged as a widely distributed receptor family. ORs are now known to be belonged to a family of seven transmembrane domain G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) expressed across diverse extra-nasal tissues, including skin, gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, cardiovascular system, liver, immune cells, and tumors. In these tissues, ORs act as metabolite- and environment-sensitive sensors that translate chemical cues into tissue-specific signaling pathways that regulate proliferati
papers.summary: This review discusses odorant receptors (ORs) that are expressed outside the nose, in tissues such as skin, gut, kidney, heart, liver, immune cells, and tumors. These extra-nasal ORs act as chemical sensors that detect metabolites and environmental cues, translating them into tissue-specific signals that regulate processes like proliferation, and the authors highlight their potential as therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening to identify FDA-approved compounds that could target monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK), an enzyme essential for viral DNA replication. By screening multiple binding pockets on the protein, the authors pinpoint candidate drugs that may be repurposed as antiviral therapies for mpox. The work provides a starting point for experimental validation of these compounds.

papers.title: TRIM2 suppresses prostate cancer progression by promoting ubiquitin-mediated degradation of DTNBP1.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men worldwide, with high mortality rates and frequent metastasis at initial diagnosis, underscoring the need to elucidate its molecular mechanisms. TRIM2, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, plays critical roles in several cancers, but its function in prostate cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the expression, biological function, and clinical significance of TRIM2 in PCa progression.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of TRIM2, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, in prostate cancer progression. The authors report that TRIM2 suppresses tumor progression by promoting ubiquitin-mediated degradation of DTNBP1, suggesting a tumor-suppressive function for TRIM2 in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Large-scale virtual screening of 17,967 IMPPAT phytochemicals identifies multiple CDR1 binders and reveals Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a putative CDR1-GSC1 dual-target lead against Candida albicans with initial in-vitro evidence.
papers.abstract: The increasing incidence of antifungal resistance in Candida albicans, mainly mediated by multidrug efflux transporters and alterations of cell-wall biosynthesis, requires the discovery of new antifungal compounds targeting multiple pathways involved in resistance. In the present study, we employed an integrated computational-experimental workflow to identify potential antifungal phytochemicals from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) database. In the virtual screening, a total of 17,967 phytochemicals were screened against the ATP-binding cassette efflux tran
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study virtually screened 17,967 phytochemicals from the IMPPAT database against the Candida albicans efflux pump CDR1, identifying several binders and highlighting Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a dual-target lead that also binds GSC1, a cell-wall synthesis enzyme. Initial in-vitro experiments support its antifungal potential, suggesting a novel multi-target strategy against drug-resistant Candida albicans.

papers.title: Experimental assessment of computationally nominated small molecules targeting the YAP-TEAD interface in Hippo pathway-altered mesothelioma cell models.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of the Hippo-YAP/TAZ-TEAD transcriptional axis is a recurrent feature of multiple solid tumors and contributes to tumor maintenance, lineage plasticity, and therapeutic resistance. Recent medicinal chemistry has shown that TEAD proteins are druggable, but the rate at which in silico screening nominates compounds that prove functionally active in cells remains poorly defined, and negative validation results are rarely reported. Here we describe an experimental assessment of a focused set of computationally nominated candidate compounds, selected from a structure-guided virtu
papers.summary: This study experimentally tested a set of computationally nominated small molecules designed to disrupt the YAP-TEAD protein interaction in mesothelioma cell models with Hippo pathway alterations. The authors report that most candidates failed to show functional activity in cells, highlighting the poor translation rate from in silico screening to cellular efficacy and emphasizing the value of publishing negative validation results.

papers.title: Bioinspired and Biomimetic Nanocarriers: Advances in Exosomes and Cell-Membrane-Coated Systems for Therapeutic Applications.
papers.abstract: The translation of nanomedicine from bench to bedside has been thwarted by the limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles including rapid mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS) clearance, lack of target specificity, immunogenicity and poor intracellular delivery. To overcome these limitations, bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers are emerging as the next generation of therapeutic platforms. Bioinspired systems replicate the core biological design principles with engineered synthetic materials and biomimetic platforms use natural biological components such as cell membranes and extracel
papers.summary: This review discusses bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers, particularly exosomes and cell-membrane-coated systems, as next-generation therapeutic platforms that overcome limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles such as rapid immune clearance, poor targeting, and immunogenicity. It highlights how these systems replicate natural biological design principles to improve drug delivery and therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Discovery of Galangin Derivatives as a Potential T-cell Leukemia Virus 1 Protease Inhibitor Through Chemoinformatics Approaches
papers.summary: This study uses chemoinformatics and molecular docking to identify galangin derivatives as potential inhibitors of the HTLV-1 protease, a key enzyme in T-cell leukemia virus type 1. The authors screen a library of natural compounds and derivatives, finding several candidates with favorable binding affinities and drug-like properties. These results suggest a starting point for developing antiviral therapies against HTLV-1, though experimental validation is still needed.

papers.title: p70S6K as a Potential Anti-COVID-19 Target: Insights from Wet Bench and In Silico Studies
papers.abstract: The onset of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 2019 sparked a global COVID-19 pandemic. This infection is marked by a significant rise in both viral and host kinase activity. Our primary objective was to identify a pivotal host kinase essential for COVID-19 infection and the associated phenomenon of the cytokine storm, which may lead to long-term COVID-19 complications irrespective of viral genetic variations. To achieve this, our study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages following SPIKE transfection over time. Among the kinases surveyed, p70S6K (RPS6KB1) exhibited a 3.5-fold
papers.summary: This study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages after SARS-CoV-2 SPIKE transfection and identified p70S6K (RPS6KB1) as a host kinase showing a 3.5-fold increase in activity. The authors propose p70S6K as a potential anti-COVID-19 target involved in the cytokine storm, supported by both wet-lab and in silico analyses.
